title: S4 Embodied scenario for the Space Unlock Tree
status: final (resolved after skeptic and advocate review)
definition: S4 Embodied = S3 Recursive cognition (cognitive work 20-50x faster from ~2029) plus general-purpose robots (humanoids and mobile manipulators run by foundation models) deployed at scale in factories, labs, test facilities, construction and off Earth, including robots helping build robots. ASSUMPTION (not inference): S3 cognition makes dexterity mainly a software problem by ~2028; field reliability still accrues on the physical clock, so usefulness is dated by hardware generation (structured multi-task ~2029; aerospace tolerances 2030-31 at leading firms).
what_S3_already_assumes: AI-run test stands and factories, physical multipliers ~1.3-1.5x; the model's S3 production-ramp factor 0.7-0.8x already cites 'AI-run factories, robotics' (model.md section 3). Specialized automation (Starfactory tile and pin robots, Rosie, AFP, autonomous-lab workcells) is S2/S3 baseline.
what_S4_adds: Only what general-purpose robots add beyond that specialized automation: labor that runs 24/7 and in parallel. Labor-bound steps compress; throughput-bound gates (capacity, replicates, facility queues, crews) become capital-bound. Physics time constants, statistics, launch windows, biology's clocks and institutions are held at S3 values for the same year in every S4 case.

fleet_trajectory.definition: Active general-purpose robots (humanoids plus mobile manipulators), end of year, M units; 5-year service life after 2026 (2 years for earlier vintages). Rebased on 2026 sequential data: AgiBot linear at ~5k/quarter (10k Mar 30, 20k Sep 24 2026); UBTech 921 full-size in H1 2026 vs 1,079 in 2025; H1 2026 global 19-25k. The 4-5 month 'doubling' is a YoY artifact of back-loaded 2025 output. Crossing years are calendar year + fraction elapsed.

path_labels.slow: Robots stay narrow and half-productive; bank consensus with typical slip
path_labels.base: 2026 = 60k; 2.3x/yr 2027-28 before broad usefulness (actuator-capacity-consistent); 2.4x, 2.2x, 2.0x as usefulness lands; 1.8x then 1.6x after 2031 with loop credit in the robot supply chain from ~2032
path_labels.fast: 2026 = 80k; working loop and wartime-style capital; post-2031 no slower than base (fixes draft inconsistency); capital passes $1T/yr ~2035

fleet_trajectory.cross_checks: Base 2031 shipments 3.35M vs infrastructure research's Epoch-anchored central 3.5M/yr; capability research central fleet 2-6M; theory 3.2M; Epoch: 1.5-3M/yr by end-2030 'clearly achievable' after a demand shock, 5-10M 'plausible'. Bank 2030 forecasts 0.45-1.2M sit between slow (0.37M) and base (1.68M). Goldman 6.5M shipments in 2035 is ~1/4 of base (26M); base 2035 output ~1/4 of world light-vehicle output by count, ~1% by mass (general). Base 2026-31 (10-month doubling) equals US aircraft 1940-44 under total mobilization, which then went flat; S4's named demand mechanism is a $20-30k robot worth ~1.5 workers with <1 yr US payback.
fleet_trajectory.draft_values_superseded: Draft base: 2026 70k, 2027 3.0x, 2028 2.6x; fleet 9.0M (2031) and 71M (2035). Now the early-onset sensitivity.

labor_share_notes: Productive human-equivalents = fleet x sector allocation x FTE per robot, where FTE per robot = (robot hours / 1,900) x productivity x productive share of fleet. Allocation 2031: manufacturing 45%, construction 4%, labs 2%, aerospace 1%; 2035: 40%, 6%, 1%, 0.5%. FTE per robot: slow 0.5/0.8, base 1.1/1.6, fast 1.4/2.0 (2031/2035), lower than the draft (0.8/1.0, 1.5/1.8, 2.0/2.4) because only productive units count. US share of fleet 10-15% (production >97% Chinese in 2026; US-China frictions), not the draft's 25%; ~13M US manufacturing workers (general). Robots reach 10% of global manufacturing labor ~2036 (base), ~2034 (fast). Values above ~50% mean the sector saturates.

rules: Physics time constants and institutions at S3 same-year values in every S4 case
Labor = S3 labor x k (k = 1.43 central 2031, 2.31 central 2035; derived)
Typical and leading programs blend labor by robot share of labor-bound steps (5-15%, 50% in 2031; 25%, 60% in 2035)

space_program.headline: Ceiling: S3 51%; S4 2031 typical 52%, leading 54%, robot-first 56-60%; S4 2035 typical 58%, leading 62%, robot-first 66-67%; floor 67-70% (2031) and 70-73% (2035); 75% with a non-robotic institutional overlay.
space_program.remaining_critical_path_reading: S3 2031: labor 28.5%, physics 35%, materials 18%, institutions 16%. S4 2035 robot-first: labor 15.7%, physics 44.3%, materials 18.2%, institutions 20.2% (physics not pre-compressed). Schedules end up set by physics and paperwork.
space_program.draft_values_superseded: Draft: typical 56%, leading 60%, robot-first 64%, 2035 68-73%, floor 69-77%. About half of the draft's S4-over-S3 gain came from raising physics, materials and institution sub-multipliers.

robot_only_split.reading: Robots (preclinical rows) add +3.7 points by 2031 and +2.9 by 2035 over S3; the rest of the S4 increment (+1.9 in 2031, +4.3 in 2035) is clinical operations, phase overlap and review speed, which are institutional or cognitive.

rows.stage: Insertion: certification, handbook, supply chain, first flight

robot_only_split.reading: Robots add ~+4.7 points (2031) and ~+4.8 (2035), mostly synthesis and replicate testing. Model-based allowables (institutional, equally available to S3) add ~+7 more by 2035. Multi-lot, multi-heat lots cannot be parallelized in time.

amdahl.material_note: S4 2035 55% assumes NASA, FAA and primes accept model-based allowables; without that ~40-45%.
amdahl.infrastructure_rules: Field-labor multiplier blended by robot share (1% typical and 30% leading in 2031 at 1.6x; 12% typical and 50% leading in 2035 at 3x). Equipment queue at S3 unless capacity outruns demand (leading 2035: 1.4x).

loop_fleet_multiplier.by_2031: ~1.0-1.2x (labor is not binding; actuators, magnets, chips, capital, certification bind)
loop_fleet_multiplier.2032_2035: Base carries loop credit (1.8x then 1.6x instead of analogue 1.2-1.3x). Loop held at 12-month doubling: 104M fleet in 2035 vs 62M base; saturating: 30M.
loop_fleet_multiplier.draft_arithmetic_superseded: Draft 2.1x by 2031 double-counted the base path's exogenous growth.

feedback_loop.verdict_2031: No material self-reinforcing loop. Fleet growth through 2031 comes from human-built, retooled factories; bound by actuators, reliability generations, magnets, chips, capital and certification.
feedback_loop.verdict_2035: The loop matters from ~2032 as robots enter reducer, screw and motor plants; capital goods (machine tools, furnaces, fabs, construction) in the mid-2030s. Not super-exponential before 2035.

caps.binds: Western chains 2026-28; Chinese supply elastic (Leaderdrive 0.43M 2025 -> >1M capacity 2026 -> >2M 2027, ~11-month doubling); rebased base path stays within it; draft's 3.0x/2.6x in 2027-28 would not
2026-30; field hours per task class; hardware generations 12-30 months

Politically now; physically base 2035 26-118 kt (1-4.5 kg/robot), fast 69-309 kt, vs ~330 kt 2025 output; explicit variable

Each domain accelerates only as fast as its slowest essential input (permits, clinical time, transformers, launches); Jones-Tonetti sigma ~0.2; Aghion-Jones-Jones

magnet_variable.reading: Magnet intensity is a design choice and the single lever that most decides 2035 fleets; base 2035 needs 8-36% of 2025 output, fast 21-94%, loop-held 16-73%. China's licensing pause lapses ~Nov 10 2026; a licensing shock would mostly hit non-Chinese makers (<3% of 2026 units) and Western deployment.

loop_labor_check.note: Draft said 1-3% of the 2031 fleet; skeptic's correction to 1.5-5.2% (draft fleet) accepted; with the rebased fleet it is ~3-8%.

feedback_loop.throughput_vs_latency: Domain progress ~ (programs, builds, experiments in parallel) / (latency per program). Robots raise the numerator roughly with the fleet where labor binds; they cut latency only where latency is labor or queue, up to the Amdahl floor. Measured in physical units, robot- and launch-adjacent domains double in under 2 years from 2027-30; large mature sectors do not before 2035.

rumor.claim: The Oct 6 2026 openai/math release is 1 of 3 solved-math dumps
rumor.finding: Unsubstantiated as of Oct 7 2026: no OpenAI statement or named reporting; repository has one commit and no batch language; OpenAI says only 'for future releases'.
rumor.likely_origin: Three OpenAI math releases in ~9.5 weeks (Aug 1 Astra ten results; Sep 8 Navier-Stokes claim; Oct 6 openai/math); SciAm report that staff remarks suggested unpublished results; Fortune report of progress on three other Millennium problems.
if_true_implies: A large backlog and fast posing and filtering (~4,000 problems posed, ~9% kept). Release dates measure disclosure policy, not throughput or capability; no doubling time is computed from them (draft's 12.6-day figure withdrawn).

Moderate evidence for upper S2 or earlier S3: shift ~10-15 points toward S3; sensitivity with recursion onset 2027. The S2-vs-S3 test is whether each release comes from a newer, stronger model weeks apart.
if_true_does_not_imply: Faster robots: AI math is a second-order input (~1.1-1.3x on the robotics timeline in S2, 1.2-1.5x in S3)
Shorter space programs: infinite cognition moves the Amdahl ceiling only 51.3% to 52.6%
Much earlier S4: an early-onset (2027) case lifts the 2031 base fleet from 6.2M to 9.0M but adds <1 point to a typical 2031 program (51.7-52.5%)

node_moves.method: Rule after review: a node gets S4 credit only if (1) its binding gate at the firm that will achieve it is labor- or throughput-bound, (2) general-purpose robots are useful there before the node's year (structured aerospace tasks 2029, tolerance-critical 2030-31, suppliers after 2031, labs 2029-31, construction trades 2031-35), (3) no hard prerequisite lands later, and (4) the credit is not specialized automation already in S2/S3. Years are earliest credible years; bands are the chance by end-2031.

method_notes: Resolved version. Synthesis of six research files compiled 2026-10-07, graph-v5.json, and the skeptic and advocate reviews. WebSearch quota exhausted; one European Commission page fetched directly; advocate-fetched URLs are marked. Fleet, labor-share, Amdahl, gate and node values are estimates computed by scratchpad/s4_model_v2.py (output s4_calc_v2.json) and this update script; sub-share splits are judgments calibrated to the model's S3 51%. Draft values are retained under draft_* keys for audit; the draft markdown is s4-embodied-draft.md.
reliability_demonstration_gate: Demonstrating mean time between interventions (MTBI) of 1,000 h at 90% confidence with zero failures needs T = MTBI x ln(10) ~ 2,300 failure-free hours per task class and environment (general). No maker publishes fleet MTBI as of Oct 2026. Analogue: driverless cars took ~13 years from the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge to commercial service.
gate_table_space_note: Calendar time as a fraction of 2026 duration. S4 2031 typical equals S3 because robots supply ~3% of aerospace production labor (base). Leading-firm values use labor x1.43, physics x1.05 (iteration share only), materials x1.1, institutions x1.0 relative to S3; 2035 leading uses x2.31, x1.15, x1.3, x1.0; S3 2035 assumed 10% below S3 2031. Draft values are kept as draft_S4_2031 and draft_S4_2035 for audit.

requalification_gate.description: Replacing human workmanship with robots on flight hardware is a process change under AS9100/NADCAP special-process rules and NASA-STD-6030 per-machine qualification; 6-24 months per process per supplier.
requalification_gate.effect: Transient penalty +3-12 months per requalified process for 2028-30 adopters (J-curve); applied as a ~1.3-point drag on the 2031 robot-first Amdahl case (57.1% -> 55.8%).
requalification_gate.evidence: Tesla Model 3 missed 2017 goal partly through over-automation (Automotive Fleet, Jan 2018); Relativity reverted to welded aluminum; Neutron slipped despite a 90-t AFP robot; Firefly 2025 ground-test explosion traced to an integration process error.

debates.resolution: Time constants and institutions at S3 same-year; iteration credit 1.25-1.5x robot-first only, booked as capital; floor 67-73%, 75% with a non-robotic institutional overlay. Hardware-rich iteration (SN8-SN15 in 147 days, 2020-21) is already in the 2026 baseline.
